what: A virtual species and a clustered survey
title: Prevalence-corrected evaluation in two routes
text: Five autocorrelated predictor layers; species responds first three. draw single clustered survey training data, fit model K = 5 covariates (three real ones plus two noise). held-evaluation set built way pseudo-absence test sets usually : enriched, every held-presence plus three times many absences. prevalence (~0.25) far landscape’s, one gap lsed corrects .
code: nx <- ny <- 80; P <- 12; K <- 5  # create sample raster template r0 <- rast(    nrows = ny, ncols = nx,    xmin = 0, xmax = 1,    ymin = 0, ymax = 1,   # projected CRS, so CV can use planar distance   crs = "EPSG:3035"    )  xy <- xyFromCell(r0, 1:ncell(r0))  ## make up some predictors.  smooth_field <- function(x, y, nh = 4, mf = 1.6) {   v <- numeric(length(x))   for (k in 1:nh)     v <- v + rnorm(1) * sin(       2 * pi * (runif(1, -mf, mf) * x +         runif(1, -mf, mf) * y) +          runif(1, 0, 2 * pi)       )   as.numeric(scale(v)) } L <- sapply(1:P, function(j) smooth_field(xy[, 1], xy[, 2]))  # create raster surface.  env <- rast(r0, nlyr = P) values(env) <- L names(env) <- sprintf("v%02d", 1:P)  # true niche: depends on v01-v03 only pres    <- rbinom(nrow(L), 1,                   plogis(-3.0 + 1.8 * L[, 1] - 1.4 * L[, 2] + 1.0 * L[, 3]                          - 0.7 * L[, 1] * L[, 2]))  # TRUE landscape prevalence pi_land <- mean(pres)  vars    <- names(env)[1:K]  # sample data from a simulated clustered survey #  to make training data n_tr <- 500; rad <- 0.22 sx <- pmin(pmax(0.5 + rnorm(n_tr, 0, rad), 0), 1) sy <- pmin(pmax(0.5 + rnorm(n_tr, 0, rad), 0), 1) tr_cells <- cellFromXY(env, cbind(sx, sy))  train <- as.data.frame(L[tr_cells, 1:K]) names(train) <- vars  train$pa <- factor(   ifelse(pres[tr_cells] == 1, "pres", "abs"),   levels = c("abs", "pres")   ) # caret needs the outcome as a factor  round(pi_land, 3) [1] 0.149 pool <- setdiff(1:ncell(env), tr_cells) pp   <- pool[pres[pool] == 1] pa   <- pool[pres[pool] == 0] ev_cells <- c(pp, sample(pa, 3 * length(pp))) # ~1:3 presence:absence eval <- as.data.frame(L[ev_cells, 1:K]); names(eval) <- vars y    <- pres[ev_cells] round(mean(y), 3) # enriched design prevalence [1] 0.25

title: Prevalence-corrected evaluation in two routes
text: survey one spatial cluster, random cross-validation folds leak neighbours train test flatter model. CAST::knndm() instead builds folds whose train--test distances match train--prediction distances across landscape, resampling reflects real extrapolation model faces, pass folds caret::train(). area applicability built training presences . pseudo-absences, scattered across environments taxon never occupies, conflate dissimilarity index. mask used keep evaluation points whose environments resemble occupied habitat, ones distinguishing presence absence actually hard. Scoring inside area applicability keeps comparison honest. model judged performs interpolating portions landscape user cares detecting new occurrences , training data model.
code: # spatial folds: train-to-test distances matched to the prediction geography tr_pts <- st_as_sf(   data.frame(     x = xy[tr_cells, 1],      y = xy[tr_cells, 2]     ),   coords = c("x", "y"),    crs = "EPSG:3035"   )  # spatial folds: create spatial CV folds // these used for # obtaining the AOA folds  <- knndm(tpoints = tr_pts, modeldomain = env, k = 5)  ## fit a model using caret m <- train(    x = train[vars], y = train$pa,   method = "glm", family = "binomial",   trControl = trainControl(     method = "cv",     index = folds$indx_train,     indexOut = folds$indx_test,     savePredictions = "final",      classProbs = TRUE     )   )  ## predict the model onto the held out test data ## giving us the prredicted probalities to go along  ## with the known preseence/ absences. ## note that caret produces a two column prediction (pres, abs) # we only need the 'pres' column to score it.  prob <- predict(m, eval, type = "prob")[, "pres"]   # AOA from CAST, referenced on the TRAINING PRESENCES only pres_rows <- train$pa == "pres" aoa_r  <- aoa(   newdata = env[[vars]],    train = train[pres_rows, vars],    verbose = FALSE   ) di <- terra::extract(aoa_r$DI, xy[ev_cells, ])[, 1] in_aoa <- di <= aoa_r$parameters$threshold # keep interpolation points only truth <- y[in_aoa] pred  <- prob[in_aoa] pi0   <- mean(truth) # in-AOA (design) prevalence

what: Route 1 “summary”: from one reported number to a decision curve
title: Prevalence-corrected evaluation in two routes
text: users probably reported PR-AUC prevalence measured (probably hidden methods; worst shared code). ap_scalar_to_prev() recovers equal-variance binormal ROC reproduces , re-prices precision landscape prevalence; nb_binormal() reads best-achievable net benefit ROC, nb_binormal_band() turns assumed spread PR-AUC plausibility band.
code: reported <- pr_auc(truth, pred) # the reported scalar, at its design prevalence pt <- seq(0.001, 0.25, by = 0.002) # threshold probabilities  rec <- ap_scalar_to_prev(reported, pi0 = pi0, pi_target = pi_land) rec[c("mu", "implied_roc_auc", "ap_target")] $mu [1] 1.893501  $implied_roc_auc [1] 0.9096996  $ap_target [1] 0.7037962  nb_sum <- nb_binormal(rec$mu, pi_land, pt)  # plausibility band: map an assumed +/- 0.04 spread in the reported PR-AUC # through to the curve (one-sided lower, the decision-relevant edge). band_sum <- nb_binormal_band(reported, pi_land, pt, spread = 0.04, pi0 = pi0)
